title: Taiwan's Maritime and Port Bureau Condemns China's Typhoon Traffic-Control Order as Illegal
detail: Taiwan's Maritime and Port Bureau formally condemned China's use of Typhoon Dolphin as a pretext to impose traffic controls on international shipping in the Taiwan Strait, saying in a statement on August 12, 2026 that China's Guangdong Maritime Safety Administration had no jurisdiction to unilaterally restrict vessel movement in what Taiwan says are international waters under UNCLOS. The bureau said it had independently issued its own maritime safety alerts and coordinated vessel-evacuation operations ahead of the typhoon without incident, undercutting Beijing's stated safety rationale. The statement followed the US State Department's August 11 rebuke of the Chinese traffic-control order, and Taiwan's Coast Guard Administration and Mainland Affairs Council both issued supporting statements reasserting freedom-of-navigation principles for the strait.

title: China and Indonesia Hold First-Ever Foreign Joint Naval Drill in Waters East of Taiwan; Taipei Calls It 'Political Manipulation'
detail: China's PLA Navy guided-missile frigate Honghe and Indonesia's frigate KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai conducted a joint navigation exercise in waters east of Taiwan island between roughly 06:30 and 09:30 local time on August 12, 2026, practicing formation sailing, maritime communications, and underway replenishment before a formal 'divergence ceremony.' China's Ministry of National Defense and state media framed the drill — the first-ever joint naval exercise between China and a foreign navy in that EEZ — as demonstrating Beijing's 'sovereign rights and jurisdiction over the exclusive economic zone east of Taiwan island.' Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council condemned the exercise as 'political manipulation,' calling it 'exercises in name, expansion in fact' aimed at 'creating a false impression before the international community that the Chinese communists have jurisdiction over waters east of Taiwan.' Indonesia's navy pushed back on Taipei's characterization, with a spokesperson describing it as a routine 'passing exercise' conducted while the frigate returned home from a port call in Vladivostok, Russia, and 'not related to war fighting.'

title: First-of-Its-Kind 'Near-Autonomous' AI-Agent Cyberattack on Taiwan Government Disclosed — 85 Accounts Breached, 2,500+ Records Stolen
detail: The Financial Times reported August 12, 2026 that Israeli cybersecurity firm Dream had detected what researchers describe as the first documented near-autonomous, AI-agent-driven cyberattack against a government target: a four-day intrusion campaign in early July 2026 against Taiwanese government systems. Attackers built an autonomous hacking platform from open-source AI-agent frameworks known as Hermes and OpenClaw, deploying up to eight agents in parallel to map 21 government systems, compromise at least 85 accounts and extract more than 2,500 personnel records with limited human intervention. Alerts on the intrusion were first issued July 20, 2026. The campaign subsequently expanded to target Taiwan's nuclear safety regulator and at least seven energy companies plus other government suppliers. Dream did not formally attribute the operation to a specific actor, but said internal communications tied to the campaign were written in simplified Chinese, pointing to likely China-linked operators; researchers cautioned the system was not '100 percent autonomous' and still required human oversight at points. Neither Taiwan's government nor Dream has publicly confirmed Chinese state attribution.
